verdict.summary: productcatalogservice began returning errors on its own (most likely a wrong/toggled configuration value - a bad feature flag or catalog/data-source setting pushed at ~08:59), and those errors propagated up through frontend to the loadgenerator.
verdict.reasoning: The alerting set is a single call chain: loadgenerator -> frontend -> productcatalogservice. The deepest alerting service is productcatalogservice, and none of its own dependencies appear (it is a leaf in this catalog), so the failure originates there rather than being inherited. loadgenerator and frontend are the noticers - errors propagate toward the caller. The onset is effectively simultaneous across all three (15s apart, which is alert-evaluation granularity), which reads like an instantaneous state change - a flag flip or config push - rather than a gradual saturation curve; a resource leak would ramp and would usually show latency first. Nothing in the blast radius suggests a slow downstream, so dependency_latency is unlikely. The catalog explicitly notes featureflagservice is absent from the graph, and the canonical failure mode for this service in demo-shaped topologies is a product-catalog failure flag / config value being enabled, which makes bad_config marginally more likely than a wholesale bad artifact.
open_questions: productcatalogservice error responses: are they fast-fail (config/flag) or timeouts (dependency)?
